note: Item codes q1..q16 = S1 xlsx headers Q1..Q16 lowercased by data/matranga_2019_hpv_knowledge.py (number-preserving; no positional step); Figure 1 numbers items 1-16 and Table 3 labels them Q1-Q16, matching the codes. Verified against Table 3 per-item group Mean(SD): 63/64 cells within 0.011, each item's nearest published row is its own (q9/q13 share means 2.63/2.75, separated by SDs 1.32/1.47 vs 1.07/1.51). Item wording transcribed from Figure 1 (image; OCR-free manual read of peerj-07-6254-g001.jpg, sha256 5d02011c...) of Matranga et al. 2019, PeerJ 7:e6254 (CC BY 4.0), incl. source non-native phrasing kept verbatim ('by who and where could you be vaccinated', 'is high the probability'). Figure is English; the study ran in a Palermo hospital with 96% Italian citizens and was almost certainly administered in Italian, but the paper never names the language and neither the paper nor its only supplement (S1 xlsx: bare Q1..Q16 headers, no labels, sheet 'Foglio1') contains Italian wording -> language=Italian inferred, fallback translated_substitute. Options 1..5 = Yes, Much, Somewhat, Little, No in printed order; direction confirmed by paper Results percentages (Q14 codes 4+5 = 21.8% vs 21.8%; Q12 code 5 = 16.7% vs 16.7%; Q11 4+5 = 44.5% vs 44.3%), but the relative order of Yes(1) vs Much(2) rests on printed order alone. resp=6 is not a printed option: Figure 1 prints five boxes (Yes/Much/Somewhat/Little/No) and the Methods say '5-level Likert scale', yet code 6 occurs 110 times across 15 of 16 items in the S1 xlsx (0 in Q9; e.g. Q8 18, Q15 16, Q10 13, Q16 13, Q13 15). Its meaning is undocumented, so its option_text is left blank. The paper's Table 3 means include 6 as a numeric value (all 32 group means reproduce only with 6 included), while its Q12 figure '16.7% had never heard of it' = 36/216, i.e. code 5 over respondents excluding code 6 -- consistent with 6 being a non-response/don't-know code. Paper-side discrepancies (not data defects): Table 3's group column headers are swapped relative to the data's Group labels (data A = age 23.1 = UAC per Table 1; published 'Ob/Gyn' column reproduces live group A), and Table 3/Results print Q7 UAC SD 1.15 where data give 1.46 (means match). Rights: THinK is the authors' own questionnaire, printed in a CC BY 4.0 article; no restriction located.
public_note: Response code 6 is not one of the five printed options (Yes, Much, Somewhat, Little, No) and its meaning is undocumented by the source, so it has no option text; the paper's own percentages suggest it marks a non-response or don't-know answer. The item wording is the English version printed in the paper; the study, run in Sicily, was presumably administered in Italian.

LANGUAGE: administered language inferred as Chinese (mainland Chinese college sample across provinces; the location field is suffixed _en, implying an English-converted Chinese field); the deposit holds 0 CJK characters in any cell or header, and there is no paper or supplement, so the fallback applies: English in base fields, language=Chinese, _translated empty. translation_source=mixed: item_text is the study's own English (study_supplied, deposit headers), instructions and option_text are the official PHQ-9 English. public_note: Respondents (Chinese college students) most likely answered a Chinese-language PHQ-9 that the deposit does not publish; the item text is the deposit's own English column headers, the instructions and response labels are the canonical English PHQ-9, and resp 1-4 are read as the standard 0-3 scoring shifted up by one (1 = Not at all, 4 = Nearly every day), an inference the deposit does not state.
